title: Path Traversal in File Construction and Zip Extraction
platform_conditions: Java SE 8+ standard library (java.io.File, java.nio.file.Path, java.util.zip); applies on all target operating systems
security_mechanism: new File(baseDir, child) treats an absolute child as a full path on most platforms, discarding baseDir entirely, and both File and Paths.get keep '..' segments; a 'startsWith' check on raw strings also fails because ./ and encoding variants normalize to the same file. ZipEntry.getName is attacker-chosen data: entries with absolute names or '..' segments (Zip Slip) escape the extraction directory unless each entry is resolved against the destination and verified to remain inside it. File.getCanonicalPath/Path.normalize/toRealPath are the mechanisms that actually collapse these variants, which is why the containment check must run on the canonical form.

source_sink_clues.source: Upload filenames, archive entry names, download/path parameters, and any path component from a request.
source_sink_clues.sink: new File(baseDir, userInput) / Paths.get(baseDir, userInput) feeding file APIs; ZipInputStream.getNextEntry with entry.getName used as the extraction target unvalidated

tracking_guards: Require the containment check on the canonical/normalized path: baseDir.toAbsolutePath().normalize() must be a prefix of candidate.normalize() (or toRealPath for symlink-aware checks) before any file API is called; require archive extraction to validate each ZipEntry name (reject absolute and '..' forms) before writing.
not_candidate_when: The child component is server-generated (UUID) or passed through File.getName-equivalent stripping, the canonical containment check rejects escapes before the file API, archive entries are validated or extracted under a resolving guard, or the base directory is not attacker-influenced and the child is a fixed constant.
synthetic_safe_example: Path p = baseDir.resolve(entry.getName()).normalize(); if (!p.startsWith(baseDir)) throw new SecurityException();
public_references: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/22.html
